title: Existence of K-flat resolutions on a ringed site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. For every cochain complex $\mathcal G^\bullet$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] there exist a K-flat complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] whose terms are flat $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] which is surjective in every degree.

proof.text: For each integer $N$, take the good truncation $\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet$. It is bounded above, so [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] gives a bounded-above complex $\mathcal E_N^\bullet$ of flat $\mathcal O$-modules and a termwise surjective quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal E_N^\bullet\to\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet$. Functoriality of the replacements supplies compatible maps $\mathcal E_N^\bullet\to\mathcal E_{N+1}^\bullet$.

Form the homotopy colimit $\mathcal K^\bullet=\operatorname{hocolim}_N\mathcal E_N^\bullet$, represented by the cone of $1-\operatorname{shift}\colon\bigoplus_N\mathcal E_N^\bullet\to\bigoplus_N\mathcal E_N^\bullet$. By [lem-pc-kflat-closure], bounded-above flat complexes are K-flat, cones and countable direct sums of K-flat complexes are K-flat, and countable direct sums of flat sheaves are flat; hence $\mathcal K^\bullet$ is K-flat and every term $\mathcal K^i=\bigoplus_N\mathcal E_N^{i+1}\oplus\bigoplus_N\mathcal E_N^i$ is flat. Since the maps $\mathcal E_N^\bullet\to\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet$ commute strictly with the transition maps, they induce a map of cones $\mathcal K^\bullet\to\operatorname{hocolim}_N\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet$, which in each degree is a direct sum of the termwise surjective maps of [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement], hence termwise surjective. The canonical map $\operatorname{hocolim}_N\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is $(x,y)\mapsto\sum_N y_N$ in degree $i$; it is surjective because $(\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet)^i=\mathcal G^i$ for $N>i$. So the composite $\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is termwise surjective.

Each $\mathcal E_N^\bullet\to\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism. A countable direct sum is the filtered colimit of its finite partial sums, so by [lem-pc-kflat-hocolim-truncations] (filtered colimits of quasi-isomorphisms are quasi-isomorphisms) the map $\bigoplus_N\mathcal E_N^\bullet\to\bigoplus_N\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The map $\mathcal K^\bullet\to\operatorname{hocolim}_N\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet$ of Step 2 is a map of cones whose two components are this quasi-isomorphism; the long exact cohomology sequences of the cones and the five lemma show it is a quasi-isomorphism. By [lem-pc-kflat-hocolim-truncations] the canonical map $\operatorname{hocolim}_N\tau_{\le N}\mathcal G^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism; composing, $\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

Steps 2 and 3 give a K-flat complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ with flat terms and a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ which, by Step 2, is surjective in every degree, as required.
